title: bevy_smokescreen: performant multiplayer-ready volumetric smokes that you can easily drop into your game
author: JayWelsh
selftext:
Hi everyone, this is a project that I've been hacking away at for a few weeks now and I feel like it's finally in a state that is worthy of a little announcement. This project is totally open source and free to use commercially for whatever you want (Apache 2.0 / MIT licensed).

https://reddit.com/link/1xis3xo/video/e5bps6yj9gyh1/player

Repo: [https://github.com/VagabondTech/smokescreen](https://github.com/VagabondTech/smokescreen)

Browser demo: [https://vagabondtech.github.io/smokescreen/](https://vagabondtech.github.io/smokescreen/)

**Full disclosure:** the project is heavily AI-assisted, so if that's an issue for you, I'm sorry.

For what it's worth, I've been a software developer for around 12 years now and this project is something I've had in mind where I wanted to specifically try to venture into a field that's totally out of my comfort zone (in order to see how far leveraging a frontier model could get me). As such, I could really use any feedback about what I can do to make the library easier to use or more useful and/or if there are any confusing parts about the API. Any pro tips in the realm of Bevy, Rust & Crate packages would be much appreciated! I am very new to this ecosystem.

These are the main focal points of this project:

***Performance***

I have tried my best to make this library as performant and optimised as possible, this means optimisation on the client side (both CPU and GPU processes) as well as the serverside CPU processes. Part of the experiment behind this library was for me to see if it would be possible for me to put something together with the help of AI that \*actually\* has decent performance, I believe that this has been achieved from my naive point of view. If anyone has  criticism regarding the performance or where you feel things are too inefficient, I'd really appreciate any critique on this front!

***Fairness***

I've done my best to keep smokes as synced up as possible, not only between clients but also for the backend to be able to accurately calculate sight lines (so that if you have bots on the backend, they won't spot you through the smoke unless they can actually see you). Bullet/explosion holes in smoke are triggered serverside to avoid high-ping players from being able to spot other players early by making holes in the smoke.

***Ease of use***

This library should be very easy to drop into an existing project, the serverside crate (\`smokescreen\`) has no Bevy dependency, the clientside crate (\`bevy\_smokescreen\`) is where the Bevy dependency lies. I've tried to keep the API clean and intuitive.

More technical details can be found in the repo's README. Thanks for taking a look, keep well! I'll hopefully be making more of these sorts of open source Bevy plugins going forward!
